result.score_rationale: All five §4 combat-core blockers (reach cap, crit read, early TTK, multi-target rule, crit gating) are closed at literal decompiled source, plus three §1 UNKNOWN-UNKNOWNS (multi-target damage rule, reach-cap↔dash relationship, hit-registration window) and half of a fourth (i-frames). Held off the 90s by four things: (a) every source cite is the ANDROID v0.682 client and parity with the web v0.717 is unproven — and already broken once, measured on frames (claim crit-meter-fill-rate); (b) duel AI/telegraphs live in EnemyPlayer.as/Enemy*.as, surveyed by L4 not here; (c) screen-shake, hitstop-beyond-i-frames and blend modes still uncatalogued; (d) three live constants in src/config/reach.ts and one in src/config/stances.ts are WRONG against the source and must be fixed before any of it is wired in.

result.score_rationale: Ledger says 34/100. Re-scored 78. All five §4 blockers resolve on disk: ① the level→stat formula is NPC.setLevel() (linear rescale + 0.9 sub-21 + a hard 1/1/1 clamp at lvl<=10); ② 403 authored <hp> rows (1..1000); ③ every attack animation ships as parta/partb/partc with explicit frame durations across 471 timed anims; ④ per-class engagement distances (50/100/400/250) plus a 24-frame decision cadence, and 118 <wave> blocks with 160 <x> spawn coords + drop-in-from-above rule; ⑤ the archer's full ballistic solve (GRAVITY=3, cos30 launch, ±4 jitter) and — refuting the blocker's premise — no reflect mechanic anywhere, only a zombie half-damage-unless-behead gate. Beyond the blockers the payload holds a 38-case ai-id→class dispatch that the shipped 3-tier AI_TIERS does not model at all. Capped at 78, not 90+, by four things: (1) every behavioural constant comes from the ANDROID v0.682 decompile — the web v0.717 payload decompile holds 652 classes and ZERO Enemy*/NPC* gameplay code, so build parity is unestablished and this is the dominant residual risk; (2) "Tengu", listed Ready in the ledger taxonomy, greps to 0 across the entire payload and script tree; (3) the 38 behaviour classes are unwritten work, not a tuning gap; (4) the 12-frame hit-lockout is a counter with no stagger animation and wants frame-side confirmation before it is treated as CONTRACT.

claims.text: The enemy level→stat formula the ledger calls "absent, not just inferred" is NPC.setLevel(): a linear rescale of the authored XML statline (factor = requestedLvl / authoredLvl, ×0.9 at or under level 20) applied identically to damage, defense and maxhp, with a hard clamp to 1/1/1 at level ≤ 10 and xp = lvl*2 + 20.
claims.quote: public function setLevel(lvl:int) : * { var factor:Number = lvl / this.level; if(lvl <= 20) { factor *= 0.9; } this.level = lvl; this.damage *= factor; this.defense *= factor; maxhp *= factor; setHP(maxhp); this.updateHealthBar(); this.xp = lvl * 2 + 20; if(lvl <= 10) { this.damage = 1; this.defense = 1; maxhp = 1; setHP(maxhp); } }

Every one of the five named blockers in the "### art-anim-audio-feel — 56" block is now resolved: (1) ALL AUDIO is recovered as 26 playable MP3 masters plus the complete mixing/trigger contract; (2) the font is identified down to its embedded font program and vendor copyright string; (3) "FX blend modes" is answered — the game sets NO blendMode anywhere, all compositing is ColorTransform + BlurFilter + ColorMatrixFilter via one small class; (4) screen-shake is fully catalogued (exact algorithm, default amplitude 30, trigger set); (5) the severed-limb death is not one variant but a gore SYSTEM with a measured 40/20/20/20 distribution, a behead flag, and a global censor switch. On top of that the animation model is settled from bytes (24 Hz keyframe stream, 21-node rig, code-added hold tails) and 14 of 18 animation blobs are proven byte-identical between the Android and web builds, so the usual Android caveat does not apply to motion. Held back from higher: the newly-opened vector art (1,949 sprites in SHS3Resource, 49 backgrounds in BGResource) was not rendered or graded this pass; audio web-parity is unproven (the web payload holds no CWS blob at all); and no test in the suite pins any of this yet.

result.score_rationale: Pass 1 of this lane already moved ui-hud 57 -> 85 on the Android decompile; I re-derived its claims 1-18 independently and they hold, so 85 is the floor, not a contested number. +3 for three things Pass 1 left open or got wrong: (a) blocker (5) goes from "half closed" to "closed except symbol geometry" — DialogBox re-assigns its layout in ActionScript every show (button.x 340 / 270+425, msgText.y 187.5 vs 220, centre-if-<=2-lines), and the battle pause is a full behaviour spec (button hidden in duel/PvP, pauseScreen raised to top, any click resumes); (b) the screen-transition durations Pass 1 declared "unheld pending a follow-up" are constants in the same file and resolve by arithmetic to 17 frames / 708 ms for each shutter and exactly 24 frames / 1000 ms for the white fade; (c) an entire UI subsystem — 19-screen, 47-menu, 139-option InteractUI UIData with inventory gates and error copy — is on disk and appears in neither the ledger nor Pass 1. Held below 90 by real gaps, not caution: no assets.swf symbol geometry exported (BattleUI symbol2952, OptionsUI symbol1133, DialogBox symbol83, SkillSlotButton symbol2915 etc. are script-only exports), no icon manifest for the 139 icon ids, HUD chrome art still sealed in the encrypted 124_Mobile_ImageResource, the 800x690 friend-bar layout is code-held but appears in zero reference frames, and "(EQ:n) UX" is still ungrounded. Separately, P1 is a correctness hit that does not change the score but changes every other lane: the string-id mapping Pass 1 used is the wrong one.

claims.text: Screen-transition durations are constants in the shipped code and resolve exactly: each black shutter takes 17 frames (708 ms) and the white fade takes exactly 24 frames (1000 ms) at the SWF's 24 fps.
claims.quote: `this.blackup.y = -240; this.blackdown.y = 480; this.blackMovtSpeed = 0; this.counter = 0;` (:143-146) then per frame `this.blackup.y += this.blackMovtSpeed; this.blackdown.y -= this.blackMovtSpeed; this.blackMovtSpeed += 2; if(this.blackup.y >= 0){ this.blackup.y = 0; this.blackdown.y = 240; if(this.counter >= 17)` (:80-88), and `this.white.alpha -= 1 / 24;` (:111). Speed applies before it increments, so displacement after n frames is (n-2)(n-1); (17-2)(17-1) = 240 exactly, which is why the gate is counter >= 17.

result.score_rationale: 31/100 is badly stale. Of the four §4 blockers: ② (map topology) is fully closed at BOTH scales — a 6×6 sector board plus a world board that is a 63×72 GIF byte-identical across the web and Android payloads (735 land territories); ③ (achievements / daily-reward / token numbers) is closed outright with 61 resolved achievements, the full 36/6/10-slot daily prize tables, and both token pools quantified; ① (server sim) is closed on MECHANICS (deploy = 100×terrain-mod, arrows = 80+rand40×mod, 7-row terrain table, structure costs, 11-rank curve, 24h advance, 39-wave battle table) and open only on hosted state; ④ (offline gold faucet) is NOT unclosable as both the ledger and the first survey pass claimed — doRebirth grants 5 Gold per rebirth and 20 at Dan 8, a 60-Gold lifetime ceiling the client itself uses as its paid-player test. verdicts.reason: The ledger bullet 'defense min-floor (EnemyLevel/4)' is CORRECT and the surveyor cited the wrong function. Damage.getMinDamage() IS the generic defense-pipeline floor: 'if(attackerlvl<=10) return 1+piercing; if(<=20) return attackerlvl/8+piercing; if(<=30) return attackerlvl/6+piercing; return attackerlvl/4+piercing;' and MCSPlayer.as applies it immediately after 'damage -= this.getDefense();' -> 'if(damage < damageObj.getMinDamage()) damage = damageObj.getMinDamage();'. For incoming damage attackerlvl IS the enemy's level, so at lvl>30 the floor is literally EnemyLevel/4. The same floor is applied at 10+ further receipt sites (EnemyWolf.as:384, EnemyShield.as:347, EnemyClone.as:222/:443, EnemyNianMonster.as:383, MCSPlayer.as:3710). The surveyor's EnemyPlayer.as:107-123 block is real (I confirmed it verbatim) but computes 'bossHP = playerhit * hitsToKillBoss' -- enemy HP auto-scaling, copy-pasted into EnemySpearElite.as:107, EnemyWolfAlpha.as:109, EnemyKanjiGuardian.as:88, EnemyElite.as:63. So 'wrong in both variable and shape' is false twice: the shape is identical (the ledger recorded the top band), and the generic pipeline really is keyed to enemy level. Acting on this correction would delete a correct L1/L2 rule.

verdicts.reason: Held. getSellAmt is byte-for-byte as quoted in Item.as and structurally identical in the web build. One correction the claim does not carry: getWeight() is STACK weight, not the itemdata <weight> field — Android returns `this.weight * this.getQuantity()`, and the web build returns `(this.weight + <weightMod>) * <qty>`. new_findings.text: uses == 0 is a sentinel meaning the item never degrades, not 'brand new': gotUsed() returns immediately when uses==0 and repair() clamps to a floor of 1, so 0 is unreachable once an item has ever worn — which is why the ladder's first branch is 'Unbreakable'.
new_findings.quote: public function gotUsed(num:int = 1) : * { if(this.uses == 0) { return; } ... this.uses += num; }  /  public function repair(num:int) : * { if(this.uses == 0) { return; } this.uses -= num; if(this.uses <= 0) { this.uses = 1; } }  /  if(this.uses == 0) { conditionStr = LangManager.getString(639); } else if(this.uses == 1) { conditionStr = LangManager.getString(392); }   [639='Unbreakable', 392='Condition: Well-Maintained']
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 (UI/HUD) + items — a builder who initialises fresh items to uses=0 makes every item permanently Unbreakable. Fresh wearable items must start at uses=1 ('Well-Maintained'); uses=0 is reserved for the unbreakable class.

new_findings.text: The elemental AoE parameter is a horizontal half-width, not a radius: the hit test compares x-distance only, so Inferno 600 / Tsunami 400 / Tornado 200 / Earthquake 50 describe a band +/-N px wide with unbounded y.

A circular-radius implementation would let an airborne or elevated target dodge an ultimate that in the original always connects. The same function is the generic melee/projectile hit test, so this applies well beyond the elemental kit.

verdicts.reason: The android numbers are right; the conclusion is a false negative that misdirects combat-core. I reproduced the surveyor's grep and it is literally true that '0.005', '1 + 0.5' and '0.5 * ' return nothing relevant in shs3_payload — because it searched for ANDROID literals and could only ever return zero. The code IS in v0.717, under different constants: §1t99s0§.as:3094 `this.§1t4417s0§ = this.§1t4420s0§ * 1.4;` (LIGHT — x1.4, NOT x1.5), :3105 `* (1 + 0.2 * this.§1t4422s0§ * 0.1)` (BALANCED), :3116 `* (0.5 + 0.4 * this.§1t4423s0§ * 0.1)` with the same <100 floor (HEAVY); the vars are fixed by the initPlayer parameter order at :194-198, the same signature as android MCSPlayer.as:182-198. §1t5957s0§.as:2721-2748 gives the whole v0.717 stance table: Light dmg 0.5+0.04m (ceiling 0.9), Balanced 1+0.02m (ceiling 1.2), Heavy flat 1.4, crit a FLAT 1.3 in all three stances, Heavy def x0.8. 'BOTH candidates were wrong … never 1.3' is exactly backwards for the target build. v0.717 crit is a FLAT ×1.3 + flat crit-damage stat, identical for every stance — no 1.5/1.2 split. verdicts.reason: The headline constant is wrong and mis-cited. The claim says maxreload = 120 frames (5s) citing §1t99s0§.as:55. Line 55 defines §1t12234s0§:int = 5*24, which is NEVER assigned to maxreload — its only two uses in the whole web bundle are §1t99s0§.as:266 and §1t122s0§.as:950, both assigning §1t4440s0§, a per-tick countdown decremented at :1244-1247. Maxreload is §1t4415s0§, and an exhaustive grep of the entire web bundle finds exactly two assignments to it, both 8*24 = 192 frames = 8.00 s (§1t99s0§.as:249, §1t4904s0§.as:77). 120 is the ANDROID value (MCSPlayer.as:239 this.maxreload = 5*24) — the exact import the claim boasts of correcting; it was re-imported via a coincidentally-equal web static. Downstream: usable range is 144 frames / 6.00 s not 72, and the 48-frame stance switch costs ONE THIRD of the usable meter, not 'two-thirds'. Natural refill is +1/tick (:1203-1205), so 0-to-full is 8.00 s. The rest of the claim (48 dead zone, 48 switch cost, slashUsage x0.5/1.0/1.5, +6 bonus refill) verified verbatim and stands. Ledger blocker (3) 'Focus numerics (max/fill/switch-cost)' is therefore NOT closed as stated.

new_findings.text: The web v0.717 crit/Focus meter's maximum is 192 frames (8.00 s), not the 120 the survey banked; usable range above the 48-frame dead zone is 144 frames (6.00 s) and it refills at +1 per tick.
new_findings.ledger_text: ③ Focus numerics (max/fill/switch-cost).
new_findings.lane_impact: L2: config must encode maxReloadFrames = 192, deadZone = 48, usable = 144, refill = +1/frame. Every derived statement in the survey's R-09 rescales: a stance switch costs one third of the usable meter, not two thirds; a 0-to-crit charge is 8.00 s, not 5.00 s. Blocker ③ is closed by THIS number, not by the survey's.

new_findings.text: In-combat stance switching has a named public gate in the web build: canChangeStance() = valid action state AND reload >= 48 — the ledger's HARD-LOCK line is dead code-level, not just caption-level.
new_findings.ledger_text: **In-combat stance is HARD-LOCKED in v0.717** ("CANNOT CHANGE STANCE"). The recreation's Focus-gated in-combat switch models **removed 2014 behavior**
new_findings.lane_impact: L2/L5: the recreation's Focus-gated switch is FAITHFUL. The gate value and the charge value are the same 48, so the rule is simply 'costs 48, refused below 48'. Two documents must be struck, not one: REBUILD_READINESS.md:158 and SHSD_MASTER_REFERENCE.md:388, which grades the hard lock [CONTRACT].

new_findings.text: The Android string table's numeric effect copy is NOT web-true: Roll's cards say 60/80/100% dodge but the shipped web build rolls against 75/85/95.
new_findings.cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_payload/scripts/§1t99s0§.as:3361-3376, with §1t120s0§.as:16 proving the skill id; contrast docs/gauntlet/L0/index/strings.json 7004/7005/7006
new_findings.ledger_text: ### skills-meters — 33
new_findings.lane_impact: Cross-lane RULE CORRECTION for every downstream lane: the survey's parity rule 'Android XML is web-true, Android AS3 is not' has a third category it does not cover — the Android STRING TABLE, which is UI copy. Any number read out of a resolved <desc> must be labelled Android-sourced and re-checked against the web bundle. This is also the one place where 'a number that reads right, from a source one build off' already bit this survey twice.

new_findings.text: A full Focus meter buys evasion in the web build: with reload == maxreload and the current stance's ultimate skill owned, an incoming attack is fully negated with 12 frames of immunity.
new_findings.ledger_text: ### skills-meters — 33
new_findings.lane_impact: L2/L5: directly contradicts the survey's 'Roll is what buys evasion, not Focus' and restores project memory's 'Focus buys evasion' as at least half right. PARTIAL because ids 1074/1075/1076 do NOT exist in skilldata.xml (real ids stop at 1068, then 1500/1501), so getStat on them likely returns 0 and the branch may be unreachable in shipped data — verify before coding, do not delete.

new_findings.text: slashUsage — the multiplicand in the whole Focus-spend model — is read off the equipped weapon with a hard floor of 48, and itemdata carries 106 <slashusage> rows.
new_findings.cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_payload/scripts/§1t1523s0§.as:2350-2358 (param 11 of the init call at :2268); reference/extracted/itemdata.xml:8044
new_findings.ledger_text: ③ Focus numerics (max/fill/switch-cost).
new_findings.lane_impact: L2/L10: this is the number that makes the meter simulable and the survey left it an opaque symbol. With max 192 / usable 144 and a 72-usage weapon: Light slash = 36, Balanced = 72, Heavy = 108 focus. Weapon choice therefore controls crit cadence — a cross-lane hook into items-equipment that no lane has claimed.

new_findings.text: Param 7 of the player init is baseReload = 48 + SPD*6 — a field distinct from maxreload, and the likely source of the survey's 120/192 confusion.
new_findings.ledger_text: ③ Focus numerics (max/fill/switch-cost).
new_findings.lane_impact: L2: the meter system has THREE reload-family numbers, not one — baseReload (48 + SPD*6, param 7), maxreload (192, hard-coded), and the 48-frame dead zone. Any config that collapses them will mis-simulate. The Android parameter names at MCSPlayer.as:182 are the Rosetta stone for the whole obfuscated web init signature and should be banked for every downstream lane.

new_findings.text: The 'Focus' skill (id 1005, the ledger's 'Replenish Focus') sets reload to maxreload - 1 in the WEB build — one frame short of crit, deliberately.
new_findings.ledger_text: ③ Focus numerics (max/fill/switch-cost).
new_findings.lane_impact: L2: the survey had this only from Android (SkillManager.as:218-219); here is the web cite, so it is v0.717 fact. Design consequence worth stating: the skill never grants the crit itself — it puts you one frame away, so a crit always costs one more tick of natural refill. Note also the string table names skill 1005 simply 'Focus', not 'Replenish Focus'.

new_findings.text: The SPEED buff multiplies SPD by 1.5 BEFORE both the cooldown modifier and the base slash length are computed — so it silently moves the 600 cooldown cap and lengthens reach.
new_findings.ledger_text: ④ SPD→cooldown formula.
new_findings.lane_impact: L2/L5/L10: the '150% SPEED' food buff is not cosmetic — it shortens every skill cooldown AND extends slash reach through the same SPD term, and under it the 600 cap bites at SPD 400. The buff family is an else-if chain (§1t99s0§.as:209-223), so exactly one is ever active.
